In 1992, President Bush signed into law the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), landmark civil rights legislation aimed at ensuring equal access for people with disabilities. Title III of the act prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in public accommodations, commercial facilities, and recreational facilities. It requires businesses covered under title III to remove architectural barriers to full participation if readily achievable, unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. Examples of readily achievable modifications include installing ramps instead of stairs, widening doorways, providing Braille signs, and using audio signals instead of visual alarm signals. Businesses are also required to make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, and procedures when necessary to ensure equal enjoyment of goods and services. For example, a hotel might provide a room on the ground floor with a roll-in shower upon request.
